references.text: The Israelites complain that they were brought out of Egypt, the same complaint as in Num 20:5
The people complain about lack of water, a parallel situation to Num 20:5
The Israelites long back to Egypt and complain about conditions in the wilderness
The people murmur against Moses and Aaron and ask why they were brought out of Egypt
Korah and his followers accuse Moses of having led them out of a land flowing with milk and honey into the wilderness
The people complain again that they were brought out of Egypt and about lack of food and water
Description of the promised land with grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranate trees - contrast to the wilderness in Num 20:5
The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey, in contrast to 'this evil place' in Num 20:5
